info.name: Warehouse API
info.description:
Auto-generated from the Doctrine/API Platform entities in src/Entity (see СХЕМА-БД.md). Run "Login" first (as an existing ROLE_ADMIN user — see RBAC note below for how the very first one gets created) — every other request inherits the collection's Bearer token from {{accessToken}}. Requests are ordered so that running each folder's "Create" request top to bottom fills in the id variables the later folders depend on (categoryId -> productId -> clientId/supplierId -> receiptId -> batchId -> ...). Receipt/Sale/Writeoff no longer accept number/status/createdBy/receivedBy/totalUsd/totalUzs on create — the server generates the number and always starts in draft. Status only changes via the dedicated POST .../change_status endpoint (not PATCH). SaleItem no longer accepts batch/total/costPrice/costCurrency/costRate — the server picks batches via FIFO automatically and computes cost/total; price is optional and defaults to Product.priceUsd/priceUzs if omitted. StockMovement, SaleItemAllocation and Profit are read-only ledgers written only by the server when a document is posted/cancelled.

RBAC: two roles exist, ROLE_ADMIN (everything) and ROLE_SALES (Sales/Payments/Clients/Debt/read-only catalog — no Suppliers/Receipts/Writeoffs/StockMovements/Profits, and purchasePrice/costPrice/costCurrency/costRate are stripped from responses). ROLE_ADMIN implicitly includes everything ROLE_SALES can do (role_hierarchy). See each folder's description for its exact requirement. Users are created only by an existing ROLE_ADMIN via "Create user (admin)" (no self-registration, no password in the body — the server generates one and returns it once). To assign/change a role on an existing user later: `php bin/console ask:roles:add-to-user`. The very first user on a brand-new database (chicken-and-egg — no admin exists yet to call the API) must be created on the server with `php bin/console ask:users:create`, not through this collection. This collection's default user ({{userEmail}}) is assumed to already have ROLE_ADMIN; {{salesUserEmail}} is a second pre-provisioned account with ROLE_SALES for testing the restricted role — login separately with it to get a second token, since the collection only stores one {{accessToken}} at a time.

item.name: Auth & Users
item.description: Login/Refresh/Is email unique are open to anyone. About me works for any authenticated user. Create user, List users, Get user by id require ROLE_ADMIN (Get/Change password also allow object == user, i.e. your own account). There is no self-registration — a brand-new database has no users at all, so the very first admin must be created out-of-band with `php bin/console ask:users:create` on the server (not via this collection). This collection's default {{userEmail}} is assumed to already exist with ROLE_ADMIN.

request.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN. No password in the body — the server generates one and returns it in the response (email + plaintext password + roles), this is the only time it's ever visible. The new user should change it afterwards via "Change password". roles must be a non-empty array of ROLE_ADMIN/ROLE_SALES (422 InvalidRoleException otherwise). Fails with 400 if the email is already taken.

exec: if (json.password !== undefined) { console.log('Generated password for ' + json.email + ':', json.password); }

request.description: Stores accessToken/refreshToken as collection variables. The collection's Bearer auth reads {{accessToken}} automatically.

item.name: Categories
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) to read. Create/Update/Delete require ROLE_ADMIN.

request.description: GET collection of Categories.
Creates a new Categories record and stores its id in {{categoryId}}.

item.name: Exchange Rates
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) to read. Create/Update/Delete require ROLE_ADMIN.

request.description: rate_date is the primary key, so nothing needs to be captured from the response.

item.name: Products
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) to read. Create/Update require ROLE_ADMIN. remainingQty is a real denormalized column (not computed on read) kept in sync by StockMovementFactory on every stock movement — no custom provider, standard Doctrine pagination/filtering (SearchFilter on name/sku/category.id, RangeFilter on minStock) all work natively. POST /products/summary (not GET — a fixed-uriTemplate GET without {id} broke API Platform IRI generation for the whole Product resource, same reason users/about_me is POST) returns { positions, low } aggregate counts for the stock-overview tiles — one SQL query server-side instead of the frontend fetching and summing the whole catalog.

request.description: GET collection of Products.

Aggregate counts for the stock dashboard tiles: positions (products with remaining > 0) and low (remaining <= minStock, including out-of-stock). Computed with one SQL aggregate query server-side instead of summing the full product list on the client. Requires ROLE_SALES.

Creates a new Products record and stores its id in {{productId}}. priceUsd/priceUzs are optional default sale prices (independently set, not derived from an exchange rate) — SaleItem.price falls back to these when omitted.

item.name: Clients
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) for read/create/update. Delete requires ROLE_ADMIN. debtUsd/debtUzs are denormalized columns on Client (not computed on read), kept in sync by DebtFactory on every Debt ledger entry — same pattern as Product/Batch.remainingQty. There is no separate /clients/debt endpoint anymore, GET /clients carries this directly with normal pagination/filtering.

request.description: GET collection of Clients.
Creates a new Clients record and stores its id in {{clientId}}.

item.name: Suppliers
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN for everything. ROLE_SALES has no access at all.

request.description: GET collection of Suppliers.
Creates a new Suppliers record and stores its id in {{supplierId}}.

item.name: Receipts
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN for everything, including change_status. ROLE_SALES has no access at all.

request.description: GET collection of Receipts.

Creates a new Receipts record and stores its id in {{receiptId}}. number/status/receivedBy/totalUsd/totalUzs/createdAt are set by the server (auto number like ПР-00001, status always starts as draft, receivedBy = current user).

Only way to change status now (no generic PATCH on Receipt). draft->posted creates a Batch per item and writes an IN stock movement for each. posted->cancelled only works if none of the batches were used yet (deletes them and their movements). posted->draft is rejected. The receipt row is locked and its status re-checked right before writing, so two concurrent change_status calls on the same receipt can't both succeed — the loser gets 422 'already changed by another request'.

item.name: Batches
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN. Read-only (GetCollection/Get only — no Post/Patch/Delete anymore, batches are only ever created server-side when a Receipt is posted). ROLE_SALES has no access. remainingQty is a denormalized column kept in sync by StockMovementFactory. product/supplier embed as nested objects (id + name) via the batch:read serialization group instead of plain IRIs, so the frontend gets product/supplier names without a separate fetch.

request.description: GET collection of Batches. Batches are created by the server when a Receipt is posted — there is no client-facing create.
Copy an id from "List Batches" (or from the Receipt Items response after posting the Receipt) into {{batchId}}.

item.name: Receipt Items
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN for everything. ROLE_SALES has no access at all.

request.description: GET collection of Receipt Items.

Creates a new Receipt Items record and stores its id in {{receiptItemId}}. No batch/total in the body — batch is created by the server only once the Receipt is posted, total is computed from price*quantity. Fails with 422 if the Receipt is not in draft status or the product is already on this Receipt.
Only quantity/price/currency/rate are patchable. Fails with 422 once the parent Receipt is no longer draft.
Fails with 422 once the parent Receipt is no longer draft.

item.name: Sales
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) for everything, including change_status.

request.description: GET collection of Sales.

Creates a new Sales record and stores its id in {{saleId}}. number/status/soldBy/totalUsd/totalUzs/createdAt are set by the server (auto number like РН-00001, status always starts as draft). rate moved from Sale to SaleItem — see Sale Items.

Only way to change status now (no generic PATCH on Sale). draft->posted re-runs FIFO allocation fresh for every item (not just re-checking the batches picked when the item was added to the draft — stock may have moved since then, so the batches actually consumed, and therefore cost/profit, can differ from what GET /sale_item_allocations showed while still draft), then writes an OUT stock movement, a realized Profit entry per allocation, and a docType=sale Debt entry per currency. posted->cancelled fails with 422 if any posted Payment still has an allocation against this sale (cancel the payment first) — otherwise writes ADJUST/reversed/opposite-sign entries to StockMovement/Profit/Debt (nothing is deleted). posted->draft is rejected. The sale row is locked and its status re-checked right before writing, so two concurrent change_status calls on the same sale can't both succeed — the loser gets 422 'already changed by another request'.
GET collection of Sale Items.

Creates a new Sale Items record and stores its id in {{saleItemId}}. No batch/total/costPrice/costCurrency/costRate in the body — the server picks batches automatically via FIFO (oldest receivedAt first, splitting across batches if needed) and computes cost/total; fails with 422 if stock across all batches of the product isn't enough. price is optional — if omitted, defaults to Product.priceUsd/priceUzs for the given currency (422 if neither was provided and the product has no default price). rate is the real UZS-per-USD exchange rate on the day of this sale line, always required regardless of currency — profit is reported in the batch's cost currency, so this rate is what converts revenue into that currency when it differs from the sale currency.
Only quantity/price/currency/rate are patchable. Changing quantity re-runs FIFO allocation from scratch. Fails with 422 once the parent Sale is no longer draft.
Fails with 422 once the parent Sale is no longer draft. Its allocations are cascade-deleted.

item.name: Sale Item Allocations
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) to read. costPrice/costCurrency/costRate are hidden from the JSON response entirely for ROLE_SALES (present for ROLE_ADMIN) via ApiProperty security — quantity/batch/saleItem are still visible.

request.description: Read-only ledger written by the server when a Sale Item is created/updated. One Sale Item can have several allocations (one per batch it was FIFO-split across), each with its own costPrice/costCurrency/costRate.

item.name: Get Sale Item Allocations by id

request.description: Copy an id from "List Sale Item Allocations" (or from the Sale Items response) into {{saleItemAllocationId}}.

item.name: Payments
item.description: Requires: ROLE_SALES (or ROLE_ADMIN) for everything, including change_status and delete. Delete only works while status=draft.

request.description: GET collection of Payments.

Creates a new Payments record and stores its id in {{paymentId}}. number/status/acceptedBy/createdAt are set by the server (auto number like ОП-00001, status always starts as draft, acceptedBy = current user).

Only way to change status now (no generic PATCH on Payment). draft->posted requires at least one allocation (422 PaymentStatusTransitionException otherwise — a payment can't be posted and then allocated later, since allocations can only be added while draft), checks that SUM(amountSpent) across allocations equals Payment.amount exactly — not just doesn't exceed it (422 InsufficientPaymentAmountException if under- or over-allocated; we don't track advance/credit balances, so a payment must be fully allocated before it can post), and that SUM(amountClosed) per sale+currency doesn't exceed that sale's outstanding debt read from the debts ledger (422 InsufficientPaymentAmountException otherwise), then writes a docType=payment, -amountClosed entry to Debts for each allocation. posted->cancelled writes the opposite-sign (+amountClosed) reversal entries to Debts — nothing is deleted, GET /debts?payment=... shows both. posted->draft is rejected. The payment row is locked and its status re-checked right before writing, so two concurrent change_status calls on the same payment can't both succeed — the loser gets 422 'already changed by another request'.
Only works while status=draft — 422 otherwise. Cascades to the payment's PaymentAllocation rows via orphanRemoval (same pattern as Delete Sales).
GET collection of Payment Allocations.

Creates a new Payment Allocations record and stores its id in {{paymentAllocationId}}. No docRate, no amountClosed in the body — the server computes amountClosed from amountSpent (in Payment.currency) and payRate: direct if currency === Payment.currency, amountSpent/payRate if this allocation's currency is USD and Payment.currency is UZS, amountSpent*payRate the other way round. payRate is required whenever currency differs from Payment.currency. Fails with 422 if the Payment is not draft, if sale is missing, or if the sale is not posted yet (no debt exists to pay against).
Only currency/amountSpent/payRate/isRounding are patchable; amountClosed is recomputed automatically. Fails with 422 once the parent Payment is no longer draft.
Fails with 422 once the parent Payment is no longer draft.

item.name: Writeoffs
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN for everything, including change_status. ROLE_SALES has no access at all.

request.description: GET collection of Writeoffs.
Creates a new Writeoffs record and stores its id in {{writeoffId}}. number/status/createdBy/createdAt are set by the server (auto number like СП-00001, status always starts as draft).

Only way to change status now (no generic PATCH on Writeoff). draft->posted re-validates stock and writes a WRITEOFF stock movement per item. posted->cancelled writes ADJUST/reversed movements with the opposite sign. posted->draft is rejected. The writeoff row is locked and its status re-checked right before writing, so two concurrent change_status calls on the same writeoff can't both succeed — the loser gets 422 'already changed by another request'.

item.name: Writeoff Items
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN for everything. ROLE_SALES has no access at all.

request.description: GET collection of Writeoff Items.

Creates a new Writeoff Items record and stores its id in {{writeoffItemId}}. Unlike Sale Items, batch is still picked manually here — no FIFO auto-allocation for writeoffs. Fails with 422 if the Writeoff is not draft, this batch is already on it, or the batch doesn't belong to the given product.
Fails with 422 once the parent Writeoff is no longer draft, or if product/batch are patched to a mismatched pair.
Fails with 422 once the parent Writeoff is no longer draft.

item.name: Stock Movements
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN. ROLE_SALES has no access (use GET /products instead for remaining quantity — remainingQty is on every Product now).

request.description: Read-only ledger — no Post/Patch/Delete anymore. Entries are written by the server when Receipts/Sales/Writeoffs are posted (type=in/out/writeoff) or cancelled (type=adjust, reversing entry with the opposite sign). Remaining quantity for a batch/product is SUM(quantity) over this table.
Copy an id from "List Stock Movements" into {{stockMovementId}}.

item.name: Profits
item.description: Requires: ROLE_ADMIN. ROLE_SALES has no access — margin is intentionally hidden from the sales role.

request.description: Read-only profit ledger — no Post/Patch/Delete. One "realized" entry per Sale Item Allocation is written when a Sale is posted (revenue - cost, reported in the batch's cost currency — revenue is converted into that currency via the sale item's rate when it differs); posting below cost yields a negative realized entry (a real loss, not a reversal). Cancelling a posted Sale writes a "reversed" entry with the opposite sign — nothing is ever mutated or deleted, so SUM(profit) WHERE sale=X always reflects the current truth.
Copy an id from "List Profits" into {{profitId}}.

Read-only client debt ledger — no Post/Patch/Delete. One entry per event that changes a client's debt: docType=sale, +amount when a Sale is posted (per currency bucket); docType=payment, -amount per Payment Allocation when a Payment is posted. Cancelling either writes the opposite-sign entry (docType unchanged) — nothing is mutated or deleted. SUM(amount) WHERE sale=X or WHERE client=X is the current balance — pre-aggregated as Client.debtUsd/debtUzs (denormalized, kept in sync by DebtFactory), no separate endpoint needed anymore.
Copy an id from "List Debts" into {{debtId}}.
